summary: Implemented provider business/developer organization details and private document requirements for AUTH-10, AUTH-10+, AUTH-11, and AUTH-12. The frontend uses the existing strict provider application contracts, sends document uploads as the API-required raw file stream with validated metadata headers, renders server-authoritative requirements and available actions, and keeps private document URLs and storage keys out of the UI.

Runtime contracts: PATCH /api/v1/provider/application/business, PATCH /api/v1/provider/application/company, POST /api/v1/provider/application/documents, DELETE /api/v1/provider/application/documents/:documentId, and GET /api/v1/provider/application.

Shared contract schemas in packages/contracts/src/provider/index.ts; provider application routes and projections in apps/api/src/modules/provider/router.ts, apps/api/src/modules/provider/service.ts, and apps/api/src/modules/uploads/router.ts.
scopeNotes: apps/web/src/features/auth/client.ts and apps/web/src/features/auth/pages.tsx were modified as explicitly authorized direct integration exceptions so the existing provider onboarding flow can reach the new organization and document screens.
The raw upload uses the existing API contract: file bytes in the request body plus validated content type, X-Document-Category, and X-File-Name headers.
The API does not expose a document list in ProviderApplicationData; the UI keeps local upload records until the next application refresh and never fabricates private URLs or storage keys.
Unsupported product fields such as service areas and property types are intentionally not rendered because they are absent from the current contract.
knownGaps: No production credentials, provider data, external storage, or live database were used; deterministic route fixtures cover the browser matrix.
The repository declares Node >=24 <25 while this environment runs Node 22.18.0; all mandatory checks passed under the available runtime.
Vite emits the existing large-chunk warning; it does not fail the build.
